chunks: Hisham ibn Salim narrated from Ammar al-Sabati, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah عليه السلام say:

Any Muslim who is living among Muslims and then apostasizes from Islam, denies the prophethood of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and rejects him, then his blood is permissible for anyone who hears that from him. His wife becomes separated from him, so she must not approach him; his wealth is divided among his heirs, and his wife observes the waiting period of a woman whose husband has died. It is upon the Imam to execute him if he is brought before him, and he is not to be asked to repent.

key_terms.ارْتَدَّ: apostatized; turned back from Islam after having been Muslim
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam, the rightful authority responsible for implementing the ruling
key_terms.دَمَهُ مُبَاحٌ: his blood is deemed licit to shed under the stated ruling
key_terms.عِدَّةَ الْمُتَوَفَّى عَنْهَا زَوْجُهَا: the waiting period observed by a widow after her husband’s death
key_terms.نُبُوَّتَهُ: his prophethood, referring to the Prophethood of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the ruling on apostasy, marriage separation, and inheritance in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning a Muslim who openly apostasizes, denies the Prophethood of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and rejects Islam. It outlines consequences in criminal law, marriage, and inheritance, and assigns enforcement of the ruling to the Imam.
